ClinicalDocument.title: SYNTHETIC RECORD, NOT A REAL MEDICAL RECORD — Progress Note 5 — Preventive Visit — Joe Louis — True-date frame: synthetic events are moved into the patient's historical lifetime. Codes, instruments, and treatments remain modern and are anachronistic.

code.displayName: Periodic reevaluation and management of healthy individual

text.paragraph: Mr. Louis is a 55-year-old man with cocaine use disorder and a cocaine-induced psychotic disorder now in remission on aripiprazole, and stage 2 hypertension on amlodipine, who comes for his yearly preventive visit one week before his ten-week review. The persecutory fears have not returned, and he sleeps six to seven hours. Two weeks ago, after an evening with an old acquaintance, he used cocaine on one day; he told the contingency management counselor at his next urine test, which was positive, and has not used since. His home blood pressure readings average 132/84. He has had no chest pain. He cannot recall a colon cancer screening test or any vaccines since his Army years. [S]

Periodic adult preventive visit completed. Health risk assessment reviewed and the prevention plan updated. HIV, hepatitis C, hepatitis B and syphilis tests at intake were negative, and he is not immune to hepatitis B. Fasting lipids at the consultation: total cholesterol 204, HDL 44, LDL 128 and triglycerides 160 mg/dL; his 10-year cardiovascular risk by the PREVENT equations is about 6 percent, below the threshold for a statin, so he chose diet and activity with a repeat panel in a year. After shared decision-making about the higher prostate cancer risk in Black men and the trade-offs of testing, he chose a PSA test: 1.3 ng/mL. [S]
Stool immunochemical test kit given, to return within two weeks.
Repeat lipid panel in one year.
Next preventive visit in one year.

Cocaine use disorder with cocaine-induced psychotic disorder, psychosis in remission (F14.250). No psychotic symptoms for five weeks; one day of cocaine use two weeks ago, reported by him and met without blame. No akathisia or abnormal movements. Safety reviewed: no thoughts of suicide or of harming anyone. [S]
Continue aripiprazole 5 mg until the ten-week review, where a taper will be discussed.
Continue contingency management and weekly cognitive behavioral therapy.

Hypertension on amlodipine (I10). Clinic 132/84 and home average 132/84 mmHg: improving, not yet at target. [S]
Continue amlodipine 5 mg; review at ten weeks with the echocardiogram.

Guideline basis: The ASAM/AAAP Clinical Practice Guideline on the Management of Stimulant Use Disorder (2023); VA/DoD Clinical Practice Guideline for Assessment and Management of Patients at Risk for Suicide (2024); CMID: Clinical Monitoring Intelligence Database, hypertension and depression, bipolar, and mood disorders monographs (2026); Medicare Preventive Services reference: visit templates, screening cascades, and documentation elements (2026); USPSTF A and B Recommendations (2026); Adult Immunization Schedule by Age (2026)

Follow-up: Ten-week review in one week with the echocardiogram. Stool test result by mail. Second hepatitis B dose in one month or more; second hepatitis A dose in six months; zoster vaccine at the next visit. Next preventive visit in one year. Next scheduled visit 1969-09-21: ten-week review: remission, the antipsychotic taper, cognition off cocaine, the echocardiogram and a one-day return to use. [S]

Voluntary advance care planning discussion of about 18 minutes, with his consent. He named a health care agent and completed a health care proxy form; the agent is recorded in the chart and is not named here. He said that what matters most to him is being treated with respect, keeping his independence, and not becoming a burden to anyone. He would want treatment for any condition from which he could recover. He chose not to record other treatment preferences today. The plan will be revisited yearly or after any serious illness. [S]
